beats.lead: Pong was never meant to be sold.
beats.text: Nolan Bushnell gave engineer Allan Alcorn the job as a secret warm-up exercise, telling him it was for a General Electric contract.
beats.note: Alcorn had never worked on a video game before.

beats.text: The paddles could not reach the top of the screen because of a defect in the circuit. Alcorn left it in on purpose.
beats.note: He reasoned that two skilled players could otherwise rally forever.

beats.name: Andy Capp's Tavern
beats.role: the bar where the prototype was tested, built around a $75 Hitachi television

beats.text: A few days in, the bar's manager called Alcorn out to fix a fault. Nothing was broken: the coin mechanism was overflowing with quarters.
beats.note: People were coming to the bar solely to play it.

beats.context: the revenue Pong consistently earned compared with other coin-operated machines.

beats.line: The first sign of a hit was a coin box too full to work.
